passages.text: So David left Gath and took refuge in the cave of Adullam. When his brothers and the rest of his father’s household heard about it, they went down to him there.
passages.sermon:
David was a man chosen by God.
David left the city of Gath.
David escaped to the cave of Adullam.
David’s brothers heard about David’s escape.
All of David’s father’s household also heard about it.
David’s brothers went down to the cave of Adullam.
All of David’s father’s household went down to him there.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֤לֶךְ דָּוִד֙ מִשָּׁ֔ם וַיִּמָּלֵ֖ט אֶל־ מְעָרַ֣ת עֲדֻלָּ֑ם וַיִּשְׁמְע֤וּ אֶחָיו֙ וְכָל־ בֵּ֣ית אָבִ֔יו וַיֵּרְד֥וּ אֵלָ֖יו שָֽׁמָּה׃

passages.text: And all who were distressed or indebted or discontented rallied around him, and he became their leader. About four hundred men were with him.
passages.sermon:
David was a man fleeing for his life.
Many people heard about David.
People who were in trouble came to David.
People who owed money came to David.
People who were bitter in spirit came to David.
All these people gathered around David.
David became their leader.
About four hundred men stayed with David.
passages.original: וַיִּֽתְקַבְּצ֣וּ אֵ֠לָיו כָּל־ אִ֨ישׁ מָצ֜וֹק וְכָל־ אִ֨ישׁ אֲשֶׁר־ ל֤וֹ נֹשֶׁא֙ וְכָל־ אִ֣ישׁ מַר־ נֶ֔פֶשׁ וַיְהִ֥י עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם לְשָׂ֑ר וַיִּהְי֣וּ עִמּ֔וֹ כְּאַרְבַּ֥ע מֵא֖וֹת אִֽישׁ׃

passages.text: From there David went to Mizpeh of Moab, where he said to the king of Moab, “Please let my father and mother stay with you until I learn what God will do for me.”
passages.sermon:
David was a man chosen by God.
David left the cave of Adullam.
He went to Mizpeh in the land of Moab.
David spoke to the king of Moab.
He said, “Please let my father and my mother stay with you.
Let them stay until I know what God will do for me.”
passages.original: וַיֵּ֧לֶךְ דָּוִ֛ד מִשָּׁ֖ם מִצְפֵּ֣ה מוֹאָ֑ב וַיֹּ֣אמֶר׀ אֶל־ מֶ֣לֶךְ מוֹאָ֗ב יֵֽצֵא־ נָ֞א אָבִ֤י וְאִמִּי֙ אִתְּכֶ֔ם עַ֚ד אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֵדַ֔ע מַה־ יַּֽעֲשֶׂה־ לִּ֖י אֱלֹהִֽים׃

passages.text: So he left them in the care of the king of Moab, and they stayed with him the whole time David was in the stronghold.
passages.sermon:
David was a leader who was fleeing from Saul.
David took his father and mother to the king of Moab.
David left his parents with the king of Moab.
The king of Moab cared for David’s parents.
David’s parents stayed with the king of Moab.
They remained there the entire time David was in the stronghold.
passages.original: וַיַּנְחֵ֕ם אֶת־ פְּנֵ֖י מֶ֣לֶךְ מוֹאָ֑ב וַיֵּשְׁב֣וּ עִמּ֔וֹ כָּל־ יְמֵ֥י הֱיוֹת־ דָּוִ֖ד בַּמְּצוּדָֽה׃ס

passages.text: Then the prophet Gad said to David, “Do not stay in the stronghold. Depart and go into the land of Judah.” So David left and went to the forest of Hereth.
passages.sermon:
Gad was a prophet.
Gad spoke to David.
Gad said, “Do not stay in the stronghold.”
Gad said, “Go into the land of Judah.”
David obeyed.
David left the stronghold.
David went to the forest of Hereth.
passages.original: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ גָּ֨ד הַנָּבִ֜יא אֶל־ דָּוִ֗ד לֹ֤א תֵשֵׁב֙ בַּמְּצוּדָ֔ה לֵ֥ךְ וּבָֽאתָ־ לְּךָ֖ אֶ֣רֶץ יְהוּדָ֑ה וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ דָּוִ֔ד וַיָּבֹ֖א יַ֥עַר חָֽרֶת׃ס

passages.text: Soon Saul learned that David and his men had been discovered. At that time Saul was in Gibeah, sitting under the tamarisk tree on the hill at Gibeah, with his spear in hand and all his servants standing around him.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul learned that people had discovered David and the men with him.
Saul was in Gibeah at that time.
He sat under a tamarisk tree on the hill at Gibeah.
Saul held his spear in his hand.
All of Saul’s servants stood around him.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁמַ֣ע שָׁא֔וּל כִּ֚י נוֹדַ֣ע דָּוִ֔ד וַאֲנָשִׁ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִתּ֑וֹ וְשָׁאוּל֩ יוֹשֵׁ֨ב בַּגִּבְעָ֜ה תַּֽחַת־ הָאֶ֤שֶׁל בָּֽרָמָה֙ וַחֲנִית֣וֹ בְיָד֔וֹ וְכָל־ עֲבָדָ֖יו נִצָּבִ֥ים עָלָֽיו׃

passages.text: Then Saul said to his servants, “Listen, men of Benjamin! Is the son of Jesse giving all of you fields and vineyards and making you commanders of thousands or hundreds?
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul spoke to his servants.
His servants stood around him.
Saul said, "Listen, men of Benjamin.
The son of Jesse is David.
Is David giving all of you fields?
Is David giving all of you vineyards?
Is David making you commanders of thousands?
Is David making you commanders of hundreds?"
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שָׁא֗וּל לַֽעֲבָדָיו֙ הַנִּצָּבִ֣ים עָלָ֔יו שִׁמְעוּ־ נָ֖א בְּנֵ֣י יְמִינִ֑י גַּם־ לְכֻלְּכֶ֗ם יִתֵּ֤ן בֶּן־ יִשַׁי֙ שָׂד֣וֹת וּכְרָמִ֔ים לְכֻלְּכֶ֣ם יָשִׂ֔ים שָׂרֵ֥י אֲלָפִ֖ים וְשָׂרֵ֥י מֵאֽוֹת׃

passages.text: Is that why all of you have conspired against me? Not one of you told me that my own son had made a covenant with the son of Jesse. Not one of you has shown concern for me or revealed to me that my son has stirred up my own servant to lie in wait against me, as is the case today.”
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul spoke to his servants.
Saul accused his servants of conspiring against him.
Saul said, “All of you have joined together against me.
None of you told me about my son’s agreement with the son of Jesse.
My son is Jonathan.
The son of Jesse is David.
None of you cared about me.
None of you told me that my son encouraged my servant to attack me.
My servant is David.
Today, my son has caused David to wait in ambush against me.”
passages.original: כִּי֩ קְשַׁרְתֶּ֨ם כֻּלְּכֶ֜ם עָלַ֗י וְאֵין־ גֹּלֶ֤ה אֶת־ אָזְנִי֙ בִּכְרָת־ בְּנִ֣י עִם־ בֶּן־ יִשַׁ֔י וְאֵין־ חֹלֶ֥ה מִכֶּ֛ם עָלַ֖י וְגֹלֶ֣ה אֶת־ אָזְנִ֑י כִּ֣י הֵקִים֩ בְּנִ֨י אֶת־ עַבְדִּ֥י עָלַ֛י לְאֹרֵ֖ב כַּיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃ס

passages.text: But Doeg the Edomite, who had stationed himself with Saul’s servants, answered: “I saw the son of Jesse come to Ahimelech son of Ahitub at Nob.
passages.sermon:
Doeg was an Edomite.
Doeg stood with Saul’s servants.
Doeg answered Saul.
Doeg said, “I saw the son of Jesse.”
The son of Jesse came to Nob.
The son of Jesse came to Ahimelech.
Ahimelech was the son of Ahitub.
passages.original: וַיַּ֜עַן דֹּאֵ֣ג הָאֲדֹמִ֗י וְה֛וּא נִצָּ֥ב עַל־ עַבְדֵֽי־ שָׁא֖וּל וַיֹּאמַ֑ר רָאִ֙יתִי֙ אֶת־ בֶּן־ יִשַׁ֔י בָּ֣א נֹ֔בֶה אֶל־ אֲחִימֶ֖לֶךְ בֶּן־ אֲחִטֽוּב׃

passages.text: Ahimelech inquired of the LORD for him and gave him provisions. He also gave him the sword of Goliath the Philistine.”
passages.sermon:
Ahimelech was a priest.
Ahimelech spoke to the LORD for David.
Ahimelech gave David food.
Ahimelech gave David the sword of Goliath the Philistine.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁאַל־ לוֹ֙ בַּֽיהוָ֔ה וְצֵידָ֖ה נָ֣תַן ל֑וֹ וְאֵ֗ת חֶ֛רֶב גָּלְיָ֥ת הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֖י נָ֥תַן לֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Then the king sent messengers to summon Ahimelech the priest, the son of Ahitub, and his father’s whole family, who were priests at Nob. And all of them came to the king.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Ahimelech was a priest.
Ahimelech was the son of Ahitub.
Ahimelech’s whole family were priests.
They all lived at Nob.
The king sent messengers.
The king ordered the messengers to summon Ahimelech.
The king also ordered them to summon Ahimelech’s whole family.
All the priests from Nob came.
They all came to the king.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח הַמֶּ֡לֶךְ לִקְרֹא֩ אֶת־ אֲחִימֶ֨לֶךְ בֶּן־ אֲחִיט֜וּב הַכֹּהֵ֗ן וְאֵ֨ת כָּל־ בֵּ֥ית אָבִ֛יו הַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּנֹ֑ב וַיָּבֹ֥אוּ כֻלָּ֖ם אֶל־ הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃ס

passages.text: “Listen now, son of Ahitub,” said Saul. “Here I am, my lord,” he replied.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Ahimelech was the son of Ahitub.
Saul spoke to Ahimelech.
Saul said, “Listen now, son of Ahitub.”
Ahimelech answered Saul.
Ahimelech said, “Here I am, my lord.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שָׁא֔וּל שְֽׁמַֽע־ נָ֖א בֶּן־ אֲחִיט֑וּב וַיֹּ֖אמֶר הִנְנִ֥י אֲדֹנִֽי׃

passages.text: And Saul asked him, “Why have you and the son of Jesse conspired against me? You gave him bread and a sword and inquired of God for him so that he could rise up against me to lie in wait, as he is doing today.”
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul spoke to Ahimelech the priest.
Saul said, “Why did you and the son of Jesse join together against me?
You gave him bread.
You gave him a sword.
You asked God for him.
You helped him so he could rise up against me.
Now he waits to attack me today.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלוֹ שָׁא֔וּל לָ֚מָּה קְשַׁרְתֶּ֣ם עָלַ֔י אַתָּ֖ה וּבֶן־ יִשָׁ֑י בְּתִתְּךָ֨ ל֜וֹ לֶ֣חֶם וְחֶ֗רֶב וְשָׁא֥וֹל לוֹ֙ בֵּֽאלֹהִ֔ים לָק֥וּם אֵלַ֛י לְאֹרֵ֖ב כַּיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃ס

passages.text: Ahimelech answered the king, “Who among all your servants is as faithful as David, the king’s son-in-law, the captain of your bodyguard who is honored in your house?
passages.sermon:
Ahimelech spoke to King Saul.
Ahimelech answered the king’s question.
Ahimelech said, “David is your servant.”
David is faithful.
David is your son-in-law.
David leads your bodyguard.
David obeys you.
David is honored in your house.
No other servant is like David.
passages.original: וַיַּ֧עַן אֲחִימֶ֛לֶךְ אֶת־ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ וַיֹּאמַ֑ר וּמִ֤י בְכָל־ עֲבָדֶ֙יךָ֙ כְּדָוִ֣ד נֶאֱמָ֔ן וַחֲתַ֥ן הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ וְסָ֥ר אֶל־ מִשְׁמַעְתֶּ֖ךָ וְנִכְבָּ֥ד בְּבֵיתֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: Was that day the first time I inquired of God for him? Far be it from me! Let not the king accuse your servant or any of my father’s household, for your servant knew nothing of this whole affair—not in part or in whole.”
passages.sermon:
Ahimelech was a priest.
Ahimelech spoke to King Saul.
Ahimelech said, “That day was not the first time I inquired of God for David.
I have done this before.
I did not do anything wrong.
May it never be that I would do evil.
King, do not blame me.
Do not blame your servant.
Do not blame anyone in my father’s house.
I, your servant, knew nothing about this matter.
I did not know anything, whether small or great.”
passages.original: הַיּ֧וֹם הַחִלֹּ֛תִי לְשָׁאוֹל ל֥וֹ בֵאלֹהִ֖ים חָלִ֣ילָה לִּ֑י אַל־ יָשֵׂם֩ הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ בְּעַבְדּ֤וֹ דָבָר֙ בְּכָל־ בֵּ֣ית אָבִ֔י כִּ֠י לֹֽא־ יָדַ֤ע עַבְדְּךָ֙ בְּכָל־ זֹ֔את דָּבָ֥ר קָטֹ֖ן א֥וֹ גָדֽוֹל׃

passages.text: But the king replied, “You will surely die, Ahimelech, you and all your father’s house!”
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul spoke to Ahimelech.
Saul said, “Ahimelech, you will surely die.
Your father’s whole house will also die.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ מ֥וֹת תָּמ֖וּת אֲחִימֶ֑לֶךְ אַתָּ֖ה וְכָל־ בֵּ֥ית אָבִֽיךָ׃

passages.text: Then the king ordered the guards at his side, “Turn and kill the priests of the LORD, because they too sided with David. For they knew he was fleeing, but they did not tell me.” But the king’s servants would not lift a hand to strike the priests of the LORD.
passages.sermon:
King Saul spoke to his guards.
The guards stood near him.
King Saul gave them a command.
He said, “Turn and kill the priests of the LORD.”
King Saul accused the priests.
He said, “They also helped David.”
He said, “They knew David was running away.”
He said, “They did not tell me.”
The king’s servants heard the command.
The king’s servants refused to obey.
The king’s servants would not harm the priests of the LORD.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר הַמֶּ֡לֶךְ לָרָצִים֩ הַנִּצָּבִ֨ים עָלָ֜יו סֹ֥בּוּ וְהָמִ֣יתוּ׀ כֹּהֲנֵ֣י יְהוָ֗ה כִּ֤י גַם־ יָדָם֙ עִם־ דָּוִ֔ד וְכִ֤י יָֽדְעוּ֙ כִּֽי־ בֹרֵ֣חַ ה֔וּא וְלֹ֥א גָל֖וּ אֶת־ אָזְנוֹ וְלֹֽא־ אָב֞וּ עַבְדֵ֤י הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ לִשְׁלֹ֣חַ אֶת־ יָדָ֔ם לִפְגֹ֖עַ בְּכֹהֲנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃ס

passages.text: So the king ordered Doeg, “You turn and strike down the priests!” And Doeg the Edomite turned and struck down the priests himself. On that day he killed eighty-five men who wore the linen ephod.
passages.sermon:
The king spoke to Doeg.
The king gave Doeg a command.
The king said, "Turn and strike the priests."
Doeg was an Edomite.
Doeg obeyed the king.
Doeg turned to the priests.
Doeg struck the priests himself.
That day, Doeg killed eighty-five men.
These men wore the linen ephod.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ לְדוֹיֵג סֹ֣ב אַתָּ֔ה וּפְגַ֖ע בַּכֹּהֲנִ֑ים וַיִּסֹּ֞ב דּוֹיֵג הָאֲדֹמִ֗י וַיִּפְגַּע־ הוּא֙ בַּכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים וַיָּ֣מֶת׀ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא שְׁמֹנִ֤ים וַחֲמִשָּׁה֙ אִ֔ישׁ נֹשֵׂ֖א אֵפ֥וֹד בָּֽד׃

passages.text: He also put to the sword Nob, the city of the priests, with its men and women, children and infants, oxen, donkeys, and sheep.
passages.sermon:
Nob was a city where the priests lived.
Doeg attacked Nob with the sword.
He killed every man in the city.
He killed every woman in the city.
He killed every child in the city.
He killed every infant in the city.
He killed every ox in the city.
He killed every donkey in the city.
He killed every sheep in the city.
He killed them all with the sword.
passages.original: וְאֵ֨ת נֹ֤ב עִיר־ הַכֹּֽהֲנִים֙ הִכָּ֣ה לְפִי־ חֶ֔רֶב מֵאִישׁ֙ וְעַד־ אִשָּׁ֔ה מֵעוֹלֵ֖ל וְעַד־ יוֹנֵ֑ק וְשׁ֧וֹר וַחֲמ֛וֹר וָשֶׂ֖ה לְפִי־ חָֽרֶב׃

passages.text: But one of the sons of Ahimelech son of Ahitub escaped. His name was Abiathar, and he fled to David.
passages.sermon:
Ahimelech was the son of Ahitub.
Ahimelech had a son named Abiathar.
Abiathar escaped.
Abiathar fled to David.
passages.original: וַיִּמָּלֵ֣ט בֵּן־ אֶחָ֗ד לַאֲחִימֶ֙לֶךְ֙ בֶּן־ אֲחִט֔וּב וּשְׁמ֖וֹ אֶבְיָתָ֑ר וַיִּבְרַ֖ח אַחֲרֵ֥י דָוִֽד׃

passages.text: And Abiathar told David that Saul had killed the priests of the LORD.
passages.sermon:
Abiathar was the son of Ahimelech.
Ahimelech was the son of Ahitub.
Abiathar escaped from Nob.
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul killed the priests of the LORD in Nob.
Abiathar told David this news.
Abiathar said Saul had killed the priests of the LORD.
passages.original: וַיַּגֵּ֥ד אֶבְיָתָ֖ר לְדָוִ֑ד כִּ֚י הָרַ֣ג שָׁא֔וּל אֵ֖ת כֹּהֲנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: Then David said to Abiathar, “I knew that Doeg the Edomite was there that day, and that he was sure to tell Saul. I myself am responsible for the lives of everyone in your father’s house.
passages.sermon:
David spoke to Abiathar.
David is the future king of Israel.
Abiathar is the son of Ahimelech, a priest.
David said, “I knew something on that day.
I saw that Doeg the Edomite was there.
I knew Doeg would tell Saul.
I am responsible for every life in your father’s house.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֜ד לְאֶבְיָתָ֗ר יָדַ֜עְתִּי בַּיּ֤וֹם הַהוּא֙ כִּֽי־ שָׁם֙ דּוֹיֵג הָאֲדֹמִ֔י כִּֽי־ הַגֵּ֥ד יַגִּ֖יד לְשָׁא֑וּל אָנֹכִ֣י סַבֹּ֔תִי בְּכָל־ נֶ֖פֶשׁ בֵּ֥ית אָבִֽיךָ׃

passages.text: Stay with me; do not be afraid, for he who seeks your life is seeking mine as well. You will be safe with me.”
passages.sermon:
David spoke to Abiathar.
David said, "Stay with me."
David said, "Do not be afraid."
Saul is trying to kill me.
Saul is also trying to kill you.
You will be safe with me.
I will protect you."
passages.original: שְׁבָ֤ה אִתִּי֙ אַל־ תִּירָ֔א כִּ֛י אֲשֶׁר־ יְבַקֵּ֥שׁ אֶת־ נַפְשִׁ֖י יְבַקֵּ֣שׁ אֶת־ נַפְשֶׁ֑ךָ כִּֽי־ מִשְׁמֶ֥רֶת אַתָּ֖ה עִמָּדִֽי׃
